{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative or shows strong bearish signals (e.g., -0.25 or below).",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent price spikes — if the last 5-7 days show upward momentum, avoid overcorrection downward.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly below historical mean over 30 days, slightly raise it to avoid underestimating rebound potential.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish (e.g., 0.00 or 0.20) — avoid over-optimism.",
    "Correct for lag: if true outcome is rising faster than forecast, adjust next period’s forecast upward by 5-10% of the gap.",
    "Avoid overshoot after sharp spikes: if model forecast exceeds true outcome by >15%, reduce by 10-20% in next period unless sentiment confirms continuation.",
    "Use sentiment as a directional filter: if sentiment is positive (e.g., 0.50+), allow slight upward bias; if negative, apply downward bias with buffer."
  ]
}
